prompt:
ATTACHED IMAGES
One image is attached to this request. It is referred to below as image 1.
Image 1 (Subject Image) is the main subject of the graphic. Treat it as the exact source, not as inspiration. Use the real person or object from this photograph exactly as it appears. Keep the identity, face and facial structure, expression, hairstyle, body shape and proportions, pose, clothing, accessories and every distinguishing detail unchanged. You may cut it out from its original background, scale it evenly, and crop or position it as the layout requires. Do not distort, stretch, squash, warp, reshape, redraw, retouch, beautify, age or de-age it. Do not replace it with a similar-looking person or object, and do not add or remove details. Only the colour treatment in the THEME section may change how it looks. Its shape, features and identity must stay exactly the same.

Create a bold editorial breaking-news social graphic.

SUBJECT
Use the attached subject photograph (image 1) as the primary subject, placed on the left half of the composition. Keep the subject photographic and naturally coloured. Do not distort, stylise or recolour the subject.

ACCENT COLOUR
Apply the selected accent colour (#1C28D4) to the bold geometric graphic elements in the background: a large vertical bar on the right, one or two horizontal rule lines, and a strong rectangular block behind the subject's head.

STYLE
Use a crisp Swiss-modernist graphic style with clean rules, strong geometric shapes, and disciplined negative space.

SPACE
Leave the right third of the composition free of the subject. This area will carry text overlaid in post-production.

FORMAT
Tall vertical 4:5 composition.

AVOID
Do not add any text, numbers, captions, logos or watermarks.

THEME
The following treatment applies to the whole finished image. Where it conflicts with any earlier instruction, follow this section.
Organise the whole composition as a contemporary editorial magazine collage with strong Swiss-inspired geometric organisation: asymmetric editorial layout, strong foreground/background hierarchy, disciplined negative space and minimal visual clutter.

Render the entire image in a single colour family based on cobalt blue (#0047AB). Use darker shades of it for shadows and lighter tints of it for highlights. Apply this to everything in the frame, including the subject, the background and all graphic elements. Keep a full tonal range from deep shadows to clean highlights. This overrides any earlier colour instruction.

Add a moderate, clearly visible film grain across the whole image. The grain should be even, monochromatic and photographic, like 35mm film.

ADDITIONAL RULES
- Do not add text, letters, numbers, logos, captions, watermarks, icons, arrows, borders, or branding.
- Do not introduce any colours outside this single colour family.
- Use the subject from the attached image exactly as photographed. Do not distort, stretch, warp, redraw, retouch or replace it, and do not change its identity, features or proportions.
